sources.title: UDI: Visits and holidays for a citizen of Kosovo
sources.officialityEvidence: UDI is Norway's official immigration authority and its country-selected guidance is current for Kosovo citizens.
sources.supportingExcerpt: you do not need a visa to visit Norway if you are a citizen of Kosovo and you hold a biometric passport.

policies.title: Kosovo biometric ordinary passports: EU short-stay visa-free entry
policies.summary: Binding EU law exempts holders of ICAO-compliant biometric passports issued by Kosovo from the visa requirement for the listed Member State short visits.
conditions: This is limited to an ICAO-compliant biometric passport issued by Kosovo. Regulation (EU) 2023/850 transferred Kosovo to Annex II and the exemption applied from 1 January 2024 because ETIAS had not begun operation first.

It is a short-visitor visa-waiver baseline only. It does not establish ETIAS timing, work, residence, study, transit, special documents, carrier requirements, national entry conditions, or final admission.
Ireland is deliberately excluded: the EU visa-list Regulation does not establish Ireland's separate national visa policy.

policies.title: Kosovo biometric ordinary passports: Norway and Switzerland short-stay visa-free entry
policies.summary: The competent Norwegian and Swiss immigration authorities expressly record a no-visa short-visit route for Kosovo biometric passport holders.
conditions: NO: UDI says Kosovo citizens with biometric passports need no visa for a visit up to 90 days. CH: SEM's current nationality register records no visa required for Kosovo for stays of up to 90 days, subject to its V12 document condition.
This excludes gainful employment, residence, special documents, destination-specific document recognition, carrier checks and final admission.
